title: Where AI Use Is Normalized, Author Seniority but Not AI Disclosure Biases Code Review
abstract: arXiv:2611.18572v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code-review tools increasingly display whether an author used AI when preparing pull requests. Recent studies report that AI disclosure makes reviewers rate otherwise identical work as less competent, with the penalty falling hardest on already-marginalized authors. In a within-subjects experiment in an AI-normalized organization, 447 software engineers each reviewed the same four code snippets under an AI-use disclosure embedded in the commit message and author-seniority labels. AI disclosure did not bias perceptions of code effectiveness or author competence, whereas a seniority label significantly biased both. Together, these findings show no detected penalty for disclosed AI use in this setting, while confirming that the author information shown in code review can still bias evaluations.

translated_title: 在AI使用常态化的环境中，作者资历而非AI披露会使代码评审产生偏差
translated_abstract: 代码评审工具日益显示作者在准备拉取请求时是否使用了AI。近期的研究报告指出，AI披露会使评审者对原本相同的工作给出更低的能力评价，且这种惩罚对已经处于边缘地位的作者影响最大。在一项于AI使用常态化组织中开展的被试内实验中，447名软件工程师分别在提交信息中嵌入AI使用披露和作者资历标签的条件下评审了相同的四个代码片段。结果显示，AI披露并未使对代码有效性或作者能力的感知产生偏差，而资历标签则对两者均产生了显著影响。这些发现共同表明，在该环境下未检测到对披露AI使用的惩罚，同时证实了代码评审中显示的作者信息仍然可能使评估产生偏差。
tldr: 在AI使用常态化的组织中，实验表明披露AI使用并不会使代码评审产生偏差，而作者的资历标签则会显著影响评审者对代码有效性和作者能力的判断。
en_tdlr: In an AI-normalized organization, a within-subjects experiment shows that AI-use disclosure does not bias code review, while author seniority labels significantly bias judgments of both code effectiveness and author competence.
